questions.:question/problem: Find the slope of the tangent to the curve $y=\sqrt{x-3}+3{x}^{3}$ at the point where $x=4.$
questions.:question/worked-solution:
To find the slope at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

Let $f(x)=\sqrt{x-3}.$ We use the chain rule in the form

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Let $u=x-3.$ Then $f=\sqrt{u}={u}^{1/2}.$ Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}=\frac{1}{2}{u}^{-1/2}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1.
$$

Multiplying the two together gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}\cdot 1 \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}} \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x-3}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the sum rule, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x-3}}+9{x}^{2}.
$$

Finally, substituting $x=4,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=4} & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{4-3}}+9(4)^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}+144 \\  & =\frac{289}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_example.:question/problem: Given that $y = \sqrt{1-x^2},$ find $\dfrac{\textrm d y}{\textrm d x}.$
canonical_example.:question/worked-solution:
We use the chain rule in the form

$$
\dfrac{\textrm d y}{\textrm d x} = \dfrac{\textrm d y}{\textrm d u}\cdot \dfrac{\textrm d u}{\textrm d x}.
$$

Here, we've used $u$ instead of $g$ for the intermediate variable. 

Let $u=1-x^2.$ Then $y = \sqrt u = u^{1/2}.$ Differentiating, we have

$$
\dfrac{\textrm d y}{\textrm d u} = \dfrac{1}{2}u^{-1/2} = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt u}
$$

and

$$
\dfrac{\textrm d u}{\textrm d x}  = -2x.
$$

Multiplying the two together gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}\cdot (-2x) \\  & =-\frac{2x}{2\sqrt{u}} \\  & =-\frac{x}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}.\end{aligned}
$$
